metadata.title: Platform Time Cryptographic Validity

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for interpreting authoritative time in cryptographic contexts to determine validity windows, freshness, revocation timing, and evidentiary sufficiency.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Cryptographic timestamps, certificate validity periods, token lifetimes, revocation freshness, and long-term validation semantics.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Defines how cryptographic systems interpret trusted time without defining time sourcing, synchronization, or enforcement mechanisms.

props.name: depends-on
props.remarks: Cryptographic validity interpretation depends on authoritative, observable, and bounded platform time.

props.name: depends-on
props.remarks: Token, certificate, and assertion lifetimes depend on secure identity primitives.

props.name: depends-on
props.remarks: Cryptographic validity semantics depend on PKI key, certificate, and revocation governance.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Provides guidance for evaluating digital signature timeliness and long-term validity. Referenced here for cryptographic interpretation semantics, not as a platform time control standard.

metadata.remarks: Platform Time Cryptographic Validity defines how security services interpret authoritative time to determine cryptographic validity, freshness, and evidentiary sufficiency. It deliberately excludes time sourcing, synchronization, and drift handling, which are governed by Secure Time leaf patterns.

components.title: Cryptographic Validity Windows
components.description: Defines acceptable validity intervals for cryptographic artifacts including certificates, tokens, and signed objects.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Reuse of expired, revoked, or not-yet-valid cryptographic artifacts.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Explicit enforcement of cryptographic validity intervals using trusted time.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Cryptographic validity intervals are enforced using authoritative time.

components.title: Revocation and Freshness Evaluation
components.description: Evaluates cryptographic revocation status and freshness (e.g., OCSP, CRLs, token issuance time) using authoritative time.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Adversary-in-the-middle attacks manipulating revocation freshness or replaying stale responses.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Evaluation of freshness windows for revocation and authentication evidence.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Cryptographic revocation and freshness checks are protected and time-bounded.

components.title: Long-Term Signature Validity
components.description: Supports determination of whether a digital signature was valid at a specific point in time, independent of current cryptographic state.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Exploitation of cryptographic algorithm deprecation or key expiration to invalidate historical evidence.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Preservation of timestamp and validation evidence enabling future verification.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Cryptographic evidence includes verifiable time context supporting non-repudiation.
